title: Alex West: Finding one product and one channel, channel-first market selection (500-subscriber Q&A)
summary: Alex West explains how he found Cyber Leads after about 20 products: pick the acquisition channel first, then a non-winner-take-all market, then the idea. He covers launching for first users, running 20 experiments inside one product, adding a done-for-you service, and shifting from artist to athlete.

principles.text: Go Channel first, then Market, then Idea, instead of building first and hunting for buyers.
principles.quote: instead of going idea Market Channel I went Channel Market idea so I went okay where do I hang out who can I reach

principles.text: Pick markets that aren't winner-take-all, are buildable solo, and show multiple players winning.
principles.quote: good Market is a market that is not a win or take market so there can be multiple players

principles.text: You only need one product and one channel; launches give a bump but you must find a repeatable channel.
principles.quote: that's all you need one product and one channel that's it

principles.text: Don't over-engineer or plan for scale early; do things by hand and go step by step.
principles.quote: don't worry about scale again scale is relative cross that uh cross that bridge when you're there

principles.text: When growth stalls, run many experiments inside your existing product rather than selling or starting a new one.
principles.quote: I run 20 experiments within cyber Le okay so this is very important many people at that point would either sell or start a new product

principles.text: Ignore what customers say they want; keep what they actually pay for.
principles.quote: I don't really I don't care what people think or tell me I care what they pay for
